related_questions.question: What is the inflation rate in France?

text_blocks.snippet: The annual inflation rate in France is currently 0.90%. This is compared to 0.60% last month and 2.50% last year. The long-term average inflation rate is 1.79%. The core inflation rate, which excludes volatile items like food and energy, is 1.60%.

list.title: Overall Inflation:
list.snippet: The 0.90% rate is lower than the long-term average, and it's the lowest it has been since February 2021.

list.title: Core Inflation:
list.snippet: The core inflation rate is slightly higher at 1.60%, but still below the long-term average.

list.title: Monthly Change:
list.snippet: Consumer prices rose by 0.6% in the latest month, the biggest increase since February 2024.

list.title: Factors Affecting Inflation:
list.snippet: Energy prices have been falling, contributing to the lower overall inflation. However, food prices are rising, and service inflation is also edging up.

list.title: Future Outlook:
list.snippet: Analysts predict the core inflation rate to be around 1.50% by the end of this quarter and to trend around 1.60% in 2026.

list.title: Recent Trends:
list.snippet: France's inflation rate has been dropping, with the current rate being the lowest in over four years, which could lead to further cuts in borrowing costs, according to Bloomberg.

list.snippet: Annual Inflation: The annual inflation rate in the Eurozone rose to 2.0% in June, up from 1.9% in May.
ECB Target: This June reading aligns with the ECB's target of 2% for price stability.
Core Inflation: The core inflation rate, which excludes food and energy prices, remained unchanged at 2.3% in June.
Services inflation was the main driver, increasing to 3.3% in June.
Food, alcohol, and tobacco inflation slowed to 3.1%.
Non-energy industrial goods inflation decreased to 0.5%.
Energy prices continued to decline, with a rate of -2.7%.
Market Expectations: Economists had anticipated the 2.0% reading for June.

perspectives.snippet: Eurostat data, from 2002 to 2024, shows cumulative inflation in euro area was approximately 56%. That means €100 in 2002 has the purchasing power of about €64 today. It takes 6.5x more euros to buy the same ounce of gold today. Euro has depreciated considerably in real terms.
